adoption.rationale: Systemd 255.4 source and a harmless live user-manager unit show that a literal semicolon in argv is serialized without escaping. The pinned drift drill capture stops at that semicolon and omits a later security flag. Adopt this narrow diagnostic-preservation guarantee under the standing autonomous policy. The pinned updater separately rejects --insecure-no-verify under systemd or non-TTY execution, so this does not claim a reachable authentication bypass.

declared_domain: systemd 255.4 systemctl-show output for a single ExecStart argv field, with no embedded NUL or newline in the serialized line, a literal semicolon inside an argv element before --insecure-no-verify, and the standard trailing " ; ignore_errors=" property separator. The scope is flag preservation by the pinned sed capture and downstream check; it says nothing about execution authorization.
guarantee: For the pinned update-unit drift drill, when systemd 255.4 serializes one effective ExecStart whose argv contains --insecure-no-verify after a literal semicolon argument, the argv extraction must preserve the flag so the downstream provenance-bypass check can report it.
input_source: The effective ExecStart argv serialized by systemctl show for an operator-configured systemd unit; the bytes are configuration-derived diagnostics and feed the drift drill security checks.
